title: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
headline: Closing the AI guidance gap in education
summary: OpenAI highlights lessons from education partnerships across EMEA regarding AI adoption, focusing on educator support, AI literacy, and evaluation. Research cited from ThinkYoung reveals a significant guidance gap where 79 percent of surveyed students use AI for homework while only 47 percent receive guidance. The report emphasises public leadership, teacher training, and evidence-based integration.
why_it_matters: Governments and educational institutions must establish clearer expectations and support structures for educators to address the growing guidance gap between student AI usage and formal instruction.

quotes.text: New research from ThinkYoung, ⁠ (opens in a new window) which examines the ways teachers and students are already engaging with AI highlights a clear guidance gap: 79% of surveyed students reported using AI for homework or assignments, but only 47% reported being shown how.
Governments need to support educators and give students clearer expectations. Below we set out how educators can be better supported to set the terms and conditions of use.

classification.significance_reason: Provides insights into educational AI adoption and the guidance gap, but lacks binding regulatory impact or direct Australian operational directives.
